newsitem.title: JORDAN: Foreign share of Jordanian stock turnover at 26pct.
newsitem.headline: Foreign share of Jordanian stock turnover at 26pct.

text.p: Foreign investors accounted for 26 percent of the Amman stock exchange's total turnover in February, the head of the bourse said on Friday.

Wahib al-Shair, director general of the Amman Financial Market (AFM), was quoted by the state news agency Petra as saying non-Jordanian Arab institutional and foreign fund trading comprised 26 percent of February's total turnover of 14.8 million dinars ($21 million), up from 21 percent in January.
Non Jordanians bought 3.9 million dinars worth of stock in February, which was nearly four times more than the amount they sold, Shair said.

Jordanian investment managers have said foreign-based Middle East funds, which list Jordan as a main component, and global funds have been increasing their activity since December especially on blue-chips.
Global funds' stake on the bourse stood at the end of 1996 at just 1.5 percent of a total market capitalisation of 3.5 billion dinars.
Trade by non-Jordanians, both Arabs and foreign, was 18 percent of 1996 total turnover of 248 million dinars.
